card.change: Refine scored parent attempt 4 with one controlled loss-and-selection change. For every sorted training or chronological-holdout frame, compute per-user class-balanced weights: an eligible user's positives receive raw weight 1, its negatives receive P_u/N_u, and degenerate users receive zero because their ordering cannot affect GAUC or nDCG; normalize all weights to global mean one to preserve the parent's regularization scale. Pass these weights to LightGBM for the chronological fit and full-data refit, and select the round count by the same weighted binary log loss instead of global AUC. Audit eligible/degenerate users and positive/negative weight totals in the checkpoint. Preserve attempt 4's binary objective, 63-leaf capacity, learning rate, early-stopping budget, last-three-date split, split-specific and full-data smoothed tables, leave-one-out encodings, metadata parsing, feature order, source-row restoration, and checkpoint-only inference.
evidence: STATE:attempt 4 is the validation-best executable checkpoint with GAUC=0.5261195586343261, nDCG@5=0.5011200600226474, and primary=0.5136198093284867; checkpoint replay passed, so the next experiment should refine rather than debug its pipeline.

STATE:attempt 4 improved both metrics over attempt 3 (GAUC 0.4391458020855132, nDCG@5 0.46472532822498236) by replacing top-truncated LambdaRank with all-row binary learning, establishing that broad pointwise supervision is the stronger parent mechanism.

Guidance:ORGANIZER_REFERENCE states that GAUC excludes all-positive/all-negative users, weights each eligible user by positive count, and ignores all cross-user order; nDCG@5 is also computed within user.

Submitted:attempt-004 uses equal row weights for binary training and chronological global AUC for early stopping. Equal row weights allocate loss roughly by user row count, while global AUC also rewards between-user calibration that the controller never measures.

EDA:user-history-density-and-support reports a median 3489 rows per user, p90 11662, maximum 49242, and user long_view rates from 0.0106666667 to 0.832. Those large size and prevalence differences make the parent loss allocation materially different from the organizer's positive-count-weighted within-user geometry.

Feedback:research_plan_review explicitly says to prefer GAUC-improving changes when controller metrics conflict because GAUC integrates over all within-user pairs, while nDCG@5 depends on only five rows per user.

EDA:tab-context-distribution, EDA:duration-scale-and-outliers, EDA:validation-cold-item-rate, and EDA:metadata-coverage-and-shape still support the incumbent feature set; this experiment deliberately leaves those features, smoothing tables, chronology, and checkpoint inference unchanged to isolate loss alignment.
STATE:attempt 1 falsified deterministic target reconstruction because evaluation_features lacks play_time_ms, so returning to the documented threshold rule is not executable.
card.falsifier: Reject executability if any weight is negative or non-finite, if weighted positive and negative mass differ beyond numerical tolerance, if predictions are not one finite score per authoritative input row, or if checkpoint-only final mode on the same label-free data_root fails to reproduce attempt predictions within controller tolerance. Reject the metric-alignment hypothesis if controller primary does not exceed attempt 4's 0.5136198093284867 by the campaign's frozen epsilon. In particular, GAUC at or below 0.5261195586343261 would show that unequal loss allocation and prevalence calibration were not limiting broad within-user ordering; if GAUC improves but an nDCG@5 loss prevents an epsilon primary gain, abandon this weighting as a standalone refinement and reserve any blend with attempt 4 for a separately frozen ensemble experiment.
card.hypothesis: Attempt 4 optimized an unweighted pointwise loss and selected rounds by global AUC even though both controller metrics depend only on ordering within user and organizer GAUC weights each eligible user's AUC by that user's positive count. This lets unequal history sizes and user-level prevalence consume gradient and early-stopping capacity that cannot improve either controller rank metric. For each eligible user, assigning raw weight 1 to each positive and P_u/N_u to each negative gives both classes total mass P_u, exactly matching GAUC's user weight while neutralizing irrelevant user intercepts. With the successful attempt-4 features held fixed, this metric-aligned loss should improve broad within-user ordering and GAUC without sacrificing enough top-five quality to offset the gain.

+def user_balanced_weights(
+    frame: pl.DataFrame,
+) -> tuple[np.ndarray, dict[str, Any]]:
+    """Match the organizer's positive-count-weighted within-user GAUC geometry.
+
+    For each non-degenerate user, every positive receives raw weight 1 and every
+    negative receives P_u / N_u. Positive and negative mass are therefore both
+    P_u for that user. All-positive and all-negative users receive zero weight,
+    as their within-user ordering is undefined or irrelevant. A final global
+    normalization keeps mean row weight at one so the parent's regularization
+    scale remains comparable.
+    """
+    users = frame.get_column("user_id").to_numpy().astype(np.int64, copy=False)
+    labels = label_array(frame).astype(np.float64, copy=False)
+    if users.size == 0:
+        raise RuntimeError("cannot construct user-balanced weights for an empty frame")
+    if np.any(users[1:] < users[:-1]):
+        raise RuntimeError("frame must be sorted by user before weight construction")
+
+    boundaries = np.flatnonzero(users[1:] != users[:-1]) + 1
+    starts = np.concatenate(([0], boundaries)).astype(np.int64, copy=False)
+    ends = np.concatenate((boundaries, [users.size])).astype(np.int64, copy=False)
+    group_sizes = (ends - starts).astype(np.float64)
+    positive_counts = np.add.reduceat(labels, starts)
+    negative_counts = group_sizes - positive_counts
+    eligible = (positive_counts > 0.0) & (negative_counts > 0.0)
+
+    weights = np.zeros(users.size, dtype=np.float64)
+    for index in np.flatnonzero(eligible):
+        start = int(starts[index])
+        end = int(ends[index])
+        negative_weight = positive_counts[index] / negative_counts[index]
+        weights[start:end] = np.where(
+            labels[start:end] > 0.5,
+            1.0,
+            negative_weight,
+        )
+
+    raw_total = float(weights.sum())
+    if not math.isfinite(raw_total) or raw_total <= 0.0:
+        raise RuntimeError("user-balanced weights have no positive finite mass")
+    normalization = float(users.size) / raw_total
+    weights *= normalization
+
+    positive_weight_total = float(weights[labels > 0.5].sum())
+    negative_weight_total = float(weights[labels < 0.5].sum())
+    if not np.isclose(
+        positive_weight_total,
+        negative_weight_total,
+        rtol=1e-10,
+        atol=1e-6,
+    ):
+        raise RuntimeError(
+            "user-balanced positive and negative masses differ: "
+            f"{positive_weight_total} versus {negative_weight_total}"
+        )
+    if not np.isfinite(weights).all() or np.any(weights < 0.0):
+        raise RuntimeError("user-balanced weights are non-finite or negative")
+
+    nonzero = weights[weights > 0.0]
+    audit = {
+        "contract": (
+            "eligible users: positive raw weight 1 and negative raw weight "
+            "positive_count/negative_count; degenerate users: 0; global mean: 1"
+        ),
+        "rows": int(users.size),
+        "users": int(starts.size),
+        "eligible_users": int(np.sum(eligible)),
+        "all_positive_users": int(np.sum(negative_counts == 0.0)),
+        "all_negative_users": int(np.sum(positive_counts == 0.0)),
+        "positive_rows": int(np.sum(labels)),
+        "negative_rows": int(users.size - np.sum(labels)),
+        "normalization": normalization,
+        "weight_mean": float(weights.mean()),
+        "weight_min_nonzero": float(nonzero.min()) if nonzero.size else None,
+        "weight_max": float(weights.max()),
+        "positive_weight_total": positive_weight_total,
+        "negative_weight_total": negative_weight_total,
+    }
+    return weights.astype(np.float32), audit
+
